jobs.title: Senior / Staff Program Manager, Sustainability Operations
jobs.description:
Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all.

Join an inclusive team passionate about one thing: using their expertise in the relentless pursuit of innovation for customers and partners. The solutions we build help make everything from virtual reality experiences to breakthroughs in neural networks possible. We do it all while committing to integrity, sustainability, and giving back to our communities. Because doing so can fuel the very innovation we are pursuing.

As Global Sustainability Program Manager, you will be an integral member of the Global Sustainability Carbon-free Group responsible for devising strategy and execution plan for APAC regions including Singapore, Malaysia and India to meet Micron’s Sustainability goals.

In this role you will need to work closely with Teams from Global EHS & Sustainability, Global Procurement, Corporate Finance, Site Facilities, Government and Public Affairs, Planning Central Team, as well as external industry agencies and consultants to fulfill the position and group responsibilities.

Responsibilities and Duties include, but not limited to:
- Establish a roadmap to advance Micron’s carbon-free electricity supply strategy to improve our Sustainability initiatives in alignment with our long-term plan.
- Assist with long-term financial analysis of projects for decision-making purposes.
- Develop and nurture relationships with key developers, regulators, and other collaborators for long-term, world-class benefits.
- Oversight of technical, market, and regulatory changes in U.S. and APAC CFE sectors incl. carbon-neutral fuel.
- Take an active role working with Procurement and Government & Public Affairs teams in regulatory processes. Influence the development of new carbon-free and balanced supply solutions offered by utilities and other suppliers.
- Develop executive reports, communications, and training materials regarding Micron's carbon-neutral electricity achievements and assist with both internal and external questions related to sustainability matters.
- Present strategy, progress, and challenges to key collaborators including management for mentorship.
- Experience using AI tools to improve project management, data analysis, reporting, forecasting, and collaborator communications.
- Ability to find opportunities for AI-based process improvements while balancing business, operational, and governance requirements.
- Demonstrated curiosity and willingness to continuously learn and adopt emerging AI technologies.
- Ability to travel domestically and internationally as needed (10 to 20% at times).

Job Requirements:
- Bachelor's degree in Environmental Engineering, Sustainability, Energy Management, Electrical Engineering, or a related discipline.
- Minimum 5 years of experience in environmental sustainability, decarbonization initiatives, renewable energy, or environmental engineering.
- At least 3 years of hands-on experience developing, sourcing, negotiating, and managing utility-scale carbon-free energy projects, including solar, wind, hydroelectric, and energy storage solutions from project development through commercial operation.
- Proven experience leading and managing multiple complex projects simultaneously , effectively coordinating with internal stakeholders, external partners, consultants, developers, utilities, and regulatory agencies.
- Strong expertise in evaluating and interpreting financial models for carbon-free electricity projects , including identification of key risks, sensitivities, and execution of technical, commercial, financial, and development due diligence.

- Demonstrated knowledge of the Asia-Pacific energy and sustainability landscape , including renewable energy procurement strategies, environmental sustainability reporting, and regional market dynamics.

- Strong understanding and practical application of sustainability frameworks and standards, including: RE100CDP (Carbon Disclosure Project)Greenhouse Gas Protocol (GHG Protocol)Environmental Attribute Certificates (EACs), Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs), and related market instruments

- Excellent stakeholder management, communication, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to influence and collaborate effectively across all organizational levels.
- Proven ability to develop and deliver executive-level reports, business cases, and presentation materials for senior leadership.
- Strong program and project management capabilities with exceptional attention to detail, organization, and execution.
- Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, PowerPoint, Word) and ability to leverage AI-enabled tools for data analysis, reporting, and presentation development.

Preferred Qualifications
- Experience with electrical grid interconnection processes and renewable energy infrastructure development.
- Knowledge or experience in emerging carbon-free energy technologies, including: Nuclear energyGreen hydrogenFuel cellsGreen ammoniaOther advanced clean energy solutions
- Experience supporting corporate sustainability goals, renewable energy procurement programs, and net-zero or carbon neutrality initiatives within multinational organizations.
- Experience negotiating Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs), Virtual PPAs (VPPAs), Renewable Energy Certificate (REC) transactions, or similar renewable energy contracting mechanisms.

jobs.title: Senior/Staff Program Manager - Sustainability Operations
jobs.description:
Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all.

Join an inclusive team passionate about one thing: using their expertise in the relentless pursuit of innovation for customers and partners. The solutions we build help make everything from virtual reality experiences to breakthroughs in neural networks possible. We do it all while committing to integrity, sustainability, and giving back to our communities. Because doing so can fuel the very innovation we are pursuing.

Sustainability Operations (Senior/Staff) Program Manager
Job Summary
Micron Technology’s vision is to change the way the world accesses information, enriching life. We show dedication to people, innovation, tenacity, collaboration, and customer focus. This dedication allows us to be a global leader in memory and storage solutions. This means conducting business with integrity, accountability, and professionalism while supporting our global community.
Micron, one of the world’s largest semiconductor companies, recognizes its environmental impact. We take proactive steps to protect the environment. Our goal is to align emissions with the Paris Agreement and keep warming below 2 degrees Celsius. We support the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 13 on Climate Action. We aim to reach net-zero greenhouse gas emissions in our operations (scope 1) and purchased energy (scope 2) by 2050. We plan a 42% absolute reduction in scope 1 emissions by calendar year 2030 (CY30) compared to the CY20 baseline. We are also working toward 75% water conservation through reuse, recycling, and restoration by CY30. Micron has committed to investing approximately $1 billion by 2028 to support these environmental goals.

About the Role
The Global Sustainability Operations (Senior/Staff) Program Manager will direct the strategy, delivery, and governance of sustainability initiatives, prioritizing on water conservation and sustainability cost management across operating locations. This role is responsible for converting long-term sustainability objectives into near-term execution plans, driving cross-functional alignment, improving financial and reporting rigor, and providing clear decision support to executive leadership.
Candidate requires close collaboration with manufacturing, facilities, sustainability, and finance partners. The ideal candidate has strong skills in program management, analytics, financial-sustainability value creation, and engaging with collaborators.
Key Responsibilities include, but not limited to:
1)Program Strategy, Execution and Water Conversation Program Management
- Lead sustainability program short term planning and implementation, with key focus on water conservation and sustainability cost management
- Develop short-term strategies and targets aligned to long-term sustainability goals.
- Build and manage governance mechanisms, reporting cadence, and performance visibility across operating sites
- Identify and implement process improvements to enhance program efficiency, governance, reporting quality, and execution effectiveness.
- Leverage digital tools, analytics, automation, and AI-enabled approaches where appropriate to improve data flow, forecasting, reporting, and support decision-making
- Partner with site and global teams to improve water performance and expand program impact
- Support compliance, audit readiness, and data assurance across relevant programs
- Present recommendations, progress updates, and arguments to executive leadership
- Drive process improvement, digitalization, and automation opportunities to enhance sustainability operations
- Coordinate external consultants, auditors, and relevant collaborators when needed

2) Sustainability Cost Program Management
- Manage sustainability cost control, including CAPEX/OPEX forecasting, budgeting, tracking, reporting, modeling, and performance assurance.
- Build and maintain cost models to support sustainability investment planning and reason development through alignment with global finance.
- Partner with relevant teams to evaluate project economics, validate assumptions, and support capital justification processes.
- Improve access to sustainability-related investments and expenditures through robust financial tracking and reporting mechanisms.
- Support executive-level decision-making by providing clear financial insights, trade-off analysis, and investment recommendations.

What We Are Looking For
- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in Engineering, Sustainability, Environmental Management, Manufacturing, Facilities, or a related field
- At least 2 years’ experience in facilities engineering, manufacturing, process operations, sustainability operations, or similar industrial environments
- Strong program management skills with the ability to lead initiatives across functions and sites
- Experience in budgeting, financial modeling, CAPEX/OPEX tracking, and developing a strong argument for projects
- Strong analytical, reporting, and dashboarding skills
- Experience with Excel and data visualization tools such as Power BI or Tableau
- Familiarity with SAP, ServiceNow, or similar enterprise tools is advantageous
- Strong communication and collaborator management skills, including executive-level presentation capability
- Experience in sustainability reporting, compliance, or audit support is preferred
- Exposure to AI, automation, or digitalization in operational environments is an added advantage

Travel:
- Ability to travel domestically and internationally as needed (10% at times).

Construction Management & Execution
- Lead the construction phase of multiple electrical projects, overseeing installation, integration, and commissioning of electrical systems.

Design Coordination
- Review and provide input on detailed electrical designs, ensuring constructability and alignment with project requirements.
- Collaborate with design engineers and other disciplines (mechanical, structural, process) to resolve design and construction interface issues.

- Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering or related field; advanced degree preferred.
- Minimum  10 years of experience in electrical engineering and construction project/program management, ideally in   semiconductor or high-tech manufacturing, data center, and pharmaceutical environments.
- Proven track record of managing large-scale, complex electrical construction programs, including installation and commissioning.
- Strong leadership, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
- Solid understanding of electrical design principles and ability to coordinate with design teams.

Skills
- Proficiency in electrical design software such as AutoCAD, Revit, and ETAP for drafting, modeling, and power system analysis.
- Strong knowledge of electrical codes and standards.
- Excellent problem-solving and communication skills.

Working Conditions
- This is a site-based role requiring full-time presence on the construction site.
- Occasional extended hours and weekend work may be required to meet project deadlines.

jobs.title: Senior Global Energy Procurement and Strategy Manager
jobs.description:
Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all .
Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever.

Micron is looking for a seasoned energy procurement expert to become part of its Global Energy Procurement group. This prominent position will guide the creation and implementation of energy sourcing plans that support key semiconductor manufacturing activities across the North American region. You will negotiate and carry out sophisticated energy transactions, develop innovative commercial structures, and secure reliable, efficient, carbon-free energy solutions that contribute to Micron's long-term growth.

Working closely with executive leadership and external collaborators, you will support future manufacturing expansion through strategic energy procurement and infrastructure planning. The ideal candidate is a commercially minded negotiator who thrives in complex environments. They can balance market fundamentals, regulatory frameworks, infrastructure constraints, and business objectives to deliver creative solutions. Success in this role requires the ability to operate independently, influence senior leaders, and structure customized commercial arrangements where standard market offerings do not meet business needs.

Responsibilities

Direct negotiations for intricate energy deals, including:
- Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs)

- Virtual PPAs (VPPAs)

- Energy Supply Agreements (ESAs)

- Utility niche agreements

- Carbon-free, renewable, traditional baseload, natural gas, and LNG transactions

- Manage transactions from market evaluation through negotiation, contracting, and implementation

- Develop commercial frameworks and strategic alliances that support Micron's energy and manufacturing objectives

- Negotiate first-of-a-kind agreements involving utilities, developers, independent power producers, infrastructure providers, energy suppliers, and government partners

- Evaluate regulated and deregulated market opportunities, including utility tariffs, transmission constraints, market access programs, and infrastructure investments

- Build financial models and arguments supporting procurement decisions, portfolio optimization, investment opportunities, and risk management

- Analyze electricity trading environments, utility rate structures, fuel markets, and regulatory developments to find opportunities and reduce risk

- Lead high-level negotiations with utilities, developers, energy suppliers, regulators, and strategic partners

- Collaborate with Legal, Finance, Sustainability, Facilities, Government Affairs, and Site Leadership to advance strategic energy initiatives

- Develop executive recommendations supporting major sourcing decisions and long-term energy strategy

Minimum Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Business, Engineering, Energy Management, or a related field

- 7+ years of experience in energy procurement, energy origination, utility management, power marketing, energy development, commodity sourcing, or related fields

- Experience negotiating complex commercial agreements

- Solid understanding of electricity markets, utility frameworks, and energy supply agreements

- Demonstrated financial modeling and commercial analysis capabilities

- Strong communication, collaborator management, and negotiation skills

- Demonstrated ability to responsibly use AI-enabled tools to improve efficiency, analysis, market research, and decision support

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience negotiating PPAs, VPPAs, ESAs, utility tariffs, natural gas agreements, LNG contracts, or carbon-free energy transactions

- Experience supporting large industrial, semiconductor, manufacturing, or hyperscale data center energy portfolios

- Proven ability to lead complex negotiations involving energy supply, infrastructure development, utility services, generation assets, or other large-scale strategic transactions

- Knowledge of North American and APAC energy markets

- Experience with nuclear, geothermal, energy storage, hydrogen, or other emerging energy technologies

- MBA or Master's degree preferred

Why Join Micron

This is an outstanding opportunity to help build the energy strategy supporting some of the world's largest semiconductor manufacturing investments!

You will direct strategic energy sourcing initiatives throughout North America, collaborating closely with energy providers, project creators, regulators, suppliers, and executive leadership. Projects could involve nuclear energy purchasing, geothermal development, utility special contracts, LNG sourcing, renewable energy purchasing, and infrastructure solutions that support significant manufacturing growth.

The successful candidate will hold a meaningful position in securing long-term energy supply, supporting manufacturing growth, and boosting Micron's global competitiveness. You will engage with energy markets, the advancement of core systems, utility strategy, sustainability, regulatory engagement, and corporate growth while influencing billions of dollars in energy spend and investment decisions.

As a world leader in the semiconductor industry, Micron is dedicated to your personal wellbeing and professional growth. Micron benefits are designed to help you stay well, provide peace of mind and help you prepare for the future.  We offer a choice of medical, dental and vision plans in all locations enabling team members to select the plans that best meet their family healthcare needs and budget.  Micron also provides benefit programs that help protect your income if you are unable to work due to illness or injury, and paid family leave.  Additionally, Micron benefits include a robust paid time-off program and paid holidays.   For additional information regarding the Benefit programs available, please see the Benefits Guide posted on micron.com/careers/benefits .

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, age, national origin, citizenship status, disability, protected veteran status, gender identity or any other factor protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws.

The PSE Strategy Program Manager drives strategic initiatives that directly enable high‑quality, scalable engineering execution in alignment with the product roadmap . This role focuses on ensuring that Product & Systems Engineering (PSE) has the right strategic clarity, domain enablement, and execution frameworks to deliver against increasingly complex and fast‑moving product priorities.

A key aspect of the role is owning and driving the AI strategy within PSE , leveraging AI and aligning engineering use cases and delivery with the broader TPG AI strategy. The Program Manager identifies where AI and emerging tools can meaningfully accelerate engineering workflows, decision‑making, and product delivery, and drives disciplined execution across multiple initiatives to maximize impact on roadmap outcomes.

Operating at the intersection of engineering strategy and execution , this role translates product and technology direction into structured programs, clear priorities, and measurable success indicators. The ideal candidate partners closely with engineering leaders to enable improved execution at scale and provide executive‑level insight that helps leadership make informed tradeoffs, ultimately strengthening PSE’s ability to deliver on the roadmap with speed, quality, and consistency.

Key Responsibilities
PSE Strategy
- Define and execute PSE strategy by aligning organizational growth with the product roadmap, while identifying global scaling needs, closing capability gaps, and optimizing team structures across PSE.
- Domain & capability growth: Lead strategic programs that strengthen PSE domain expertise, cross‑functional alignment, and organizational effectiveness from concept through execution.
- Strategically manage AI roadmap within PSE, aligning goals and execution with broader TPG AI strategy. Ensure cohesive delivery, strong governance, and measurable impact in support of enterprise AI objectives across multiple AI initiatives.
- AI deployment & future of work: Drive adoption of AI‑enabled tools and new ways of working to prepare PSE for evolving roles, skills, and operating models.
- Establish KPIs and success metrics that measure organizational impact, adoption, and business outcomes.
- Partner with PSE leaders to equip managers with scalable structures, tools, and processes—leveraging standardization, automation, and AI‑assisted decision support—to grow teams and improve end‑to‑end organizational effectiveness.
- Build executive-ready progress updates and recommendations that inform leadership decisions.

Required Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree in Business, Program Management, Strategy, Organizational Effectiveness, or a related field — or an equivalent combination of education and professional experience.
- 7+ years of experience in program management, strategy execution, or organizational/business operations roles.
- Demonstrated experience leading large, cross-functional strategy programs at scale.
- Proven ability to operate with a high degree of autonomy and influence across global, matrixed organizations.
- Strong understanding of how complex organizations operate, scale, and deliver results.

Preferred Qualifications
- Experience leading organizational, or business strategy programs within a technical or engineering organization.
- Background in business operations, chief-of-staff functions, strategic planning, or large-scale program management.
- Exposure to AI, automation, or digital transformation programs and their impact on how organizations work.
- Familiarity with product development environments (semiconductor, hardware, or complex systems is a plus).
- Strong data mindset with experience defining and tracking KPIs tied to organizational outcomes and business impact.

Key Skills & Attributes
- Strategic thinker with strong execution discipline
- Comfortable operating at both executive and working levels
- Strong stakeholder management and influence skills
- Excellent written and verbal communication, including executive-level storytelling
- Bias for structure — able to translate ambiguity into clear programs and outcomes
- Forward-looking mindset with curiosity around AI and the future of work
- Business and organizational acumen, with a focus on scale and growth

Impact of the Role
This role is critical to enabling PSE to scale as an organization and execute against an expanding product roadmap in an environment increasingly shaped by AI and new ways of working. Success will be measured through stronger organizational readiness, effective program execution, improved operational efficiency, and tighter alignment between PSE's organizational strategy and the future direction of the business.

jobs.title: Global Facilities Program Manager (PMO)
jobs.description:
Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all.

Join an inclusive team passionate about one thing: using their expertise in the relentless pursuit of innovation for customers and partners. The solutions we build help make everything from virtual reality experiences to breakthroughs in neural networks possible. We do it all while committing to integrity, sustainability, and giving back to our communities. Because doing so can fuel the very innovation we are pursuing.

Description
As a Global Facilities Senior Program Manager, you will work closely with all the major functional organizations within Global Facilities, & with the world-wide site Facilities, FE Strategic Program (FE PMO) team and other major corporate organizations to drive systems projects/programs from initiation to completion. These projects/programs are critical to the success of Facilities and the overall network.

- Lead and orchestrate cross‑functional program and portfolio execution by partnering with Global and Site Facilities, PMO, IT, system owners, and developers to design, standardize, and deploy global reports, enterprise programs, and scalable business processes for a geographically distributed, multicultural organization.

- Establish and enforce PMO governance frameworks across projects, programs, and portfolios, including prioritization, intake, roadmap planning, dependency management, and change control—while continuously re‑aligning execution priorities to evolving business needs and strategic direction.

- Define, implement, and sustain enterprise performance management practices by partnering with metrics owners and systems teams to design, publish, and govern routine and ad‑hoc dashboards and reports that enable leadership visibility, data‑driven decision‑making, and portfolio health monitoring.

- Drive accountability and continuous improvement through structured communication, milestone tracking, risk and issue management, executive‑ready status reporting, and disciplined use of metrics to measure outcomes, identify gaps, and ensure delivery against commitments.

- Serve as the accountable owner for Global Facilities platforms and solutions (e.g., SharePoint, EDC, SQL servers, Microsoft Teams groups, web interfaces), ensuring disciplined system governance, lifecycle management, standardized operating models, and effective adoption through clear administrative controls and professional advisory support.

Qualifications
The successful candidate for this position will have:
- Excellent skills for leading or facilitating multi-organizational teams to success on complex multidimensional projects/programs
- Excellent communication skills to build teams comprised of key skills, to drive progress to plan and to get management support and buy-in for complex projects/programs
- Strong teammate to effectively collaborate with multi-functional organizations and proven track record, interpersonal, and customer service skill to comfortably work across boundaries and geographies.
- Professional, organized, meticulous, strong analytical, problem-solving, and facilitation skills. Able to independently complete tasks and adapt to constantly evolving environment.
- 5 or more years of Facilities Semiconductor industry engineering experience will be preferred
- Project/Program management experiences are preferable
- Skilled in the creation and management of projects/programs (Power BI, Tableau reports, SharePoint Online, etc) and Microsoft Office suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Outlook, Project, Power Automate, PowerApps).
- Working knowledge and drive quality programs such as MOC, FMEA, Calibration, GDMS, Error-Proofing, etc

Education
- Bachelor’s degree in engineering or equivalent

Workplace
- Travel Required          : Yes – Domestic and International travel as required by business needs
- Environment               : Office
- Shift                            : Normal shift (8+ hour)

Req. ID:
JR70144 Engineer - Central Strategic Planning

At Micron, we are searching for an outstanding Engineer - Global Quality (GQ) Operation Lab Strategic Planning, to join our highly skilled team.

As strategic planners, we are responsible to own and run the assessment and the planning of securing GQ Ops resources: the required budget, capacity, and headcount, using engineering skills. Constantly be aware of both the product roadmap and the operation needs to suggest and coordinate the best path forward plan with relevant partners in the execution team as well as the management team.

Be a fast learner in understanding operation metrics, indices, and process to translate the operations needs for long term two-to-three-year plan. We identify risk to the strategic plan early and discuss with key partners for the most optional mitigation and preventive plan.

We need to be quickly familiar with the detail business process on how to secure the required said resources. We apply strong collaborations with various partners from manufacturing team, lab operation team, engineering team, equipment support team, procurement team and finance team.

We have plenty of opportunity to be involved in the Digital Transformation for GQ Ops central planning systems to provide near real time headcount, capacity, and budget resources requirements. We will be influencing how the system is designed to check performance to plan to ensure that the long-term-plan is updated to the latest situations with each cadence. This will culminate in enabling the team to provide prompt response on the strategic assessment, planning and improvements. You will be making a difference in the team experience as well as (internal) customer experience.

We look forward having an engaged, fruitful, and meaningful journey together! Join us now!

Responsibilities and Tasks
- Take ownership of the offloading and optimization process across countries for GQ operations. Collaborate with global labs, engineering teams, equipment support, and partner central teams.
- Own and handle centralized quarterly strategic planning budget, capacity and headcount statement of up to 3 years horizon for Global Quality Lab Operations. - Comprehend operations needs including changes in the pipeline.
- Comprehend Micron product roadmap needs.
- Suggest and initiate potential improvements in the planning of the resources required through collaboration with partners from various team such as engineering, production, equipment support, procurement, and finance team.
- Setup and own global equipment and headcount modelling

- Digital Transformation for GQ Ops central planning systems - Analyze current and the required future processes and systems that is instrumental to give insights on (1) resources requirement and (2) opportunities for improvement that support business needs.
- Initiate collaboration to scope out system requirements.
- Collaborate with main partners to plan for digitalizing systems.
- Communicate status of projects.
- Report issues, risks, changes, and drive initiatives for recovery, mitigation, and preventive measures.
- Assist with documentation and training needs for new processes.
- Manages projects to ensure desired results are completed within the required timeframe.

Requirements:
- Bachelor’s or master’s degree in industrial engineering & management, engineering, supply chain, or related field and/or equivalent experience.
- Two years of experience in planning or planning-related function, preferably within Micron.
- Preferably with experience or at least willing to learn, in the following areas: - Familiar with database management system
- Strong skills in data presentation (Tableau, Power BI).

- Strong critical and analytical thinking skill.
- Strong problem-solving skills with ability to multi-task and handle numerous projects simultaneously.
- Able to work in numerous areas of a development cycle as part of a team or independently.
- High adaptability and flexibility to take care of variety of problems in a fast-paced environment.
- Strong interpersonal skills.
- Excellent oral and written communication skills and presentation skills.
- Validated leadership skills. - Able to collaborate in various cultures to drive projects forward and to completion.
- Able to articulate problem statement and address root cause.
- Able to apply creativity and innovation into solutioning as needed.

- Self-motivated, strong ownership and ability to work independently with minimal supervision.
- Very high attention to detail and data accuracy and quality.

jobs.title: Principal AI Strategy Architect
jobs.description:
Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all .
Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever.

Micron’s IT organization seeks a Principal Architect to lead our AI Strategy and Emerging Systems efforts. In this strategic role, you will research, investigate, track, and evaluate innovative AI capabilities. These include generative LLMs, agentic systems, and multimodal AI. You will rapidly prototype proof-of-concepts and translate innovations into clear business opportunities supported by accurate risk controls. You will partner with AI Enablement, IT, and business teams to ensure our AI roadmap stays on the forefront while upholding Micron’s values and governance standards.

Responsibilities:
- Discover, track, and assess emerging AI capabilities and trends: (GenAI, agentic systems, multimodal, retrieval, model customization, inference optimization, governance tooling, and security patterns), translating developments into relevance for Micron’s business and technology landscape.

- Architect AI Solutions & Platforms:  Define and evolve enterprise AI architecture patterns (cloud/hybrid, data pipelines, MLOps) for large-scale generative AI and modeling workloads. Design AI system integrations (LLMs, RAG, agents) with Micron’s Microsoft 365 and cloud platforms.

- Innovate and Prototype:  Lead rapid experimentation by building AI proof-of-concepts (e.g. chatbots, predictive analytics, AI assistants). Validate feasibility, performance, and cost; recommend scale-up or pivot decisions based on results.

- Assess Value & Risk:  Identify high-impact use cases across functions (manufacturing, supply chain, R&D, etc.) and quantify business value. Simultaneously evaluate data security, IP protection, privacy, fairness, and compliance, ensuring responsible AI practices in all initiatives.

- Enable Responsible AI:  Develop standards and guardrails for model selection, prompt/data engineering, and human-in-the-loop processes. Advise on red-teaming, adversarial testing, and monitoring to mitigate AI risks.

- Communicate Insights:  Translate complex AI developments into concise briefings for executives and partners. Provide deep technical mentorship to engineering teams and mentor stakeholders on AI capabilities and limitations.

- Drive AI Strategy:  Partner with AI governance and IT leadership to update AI strategy and policies. Recommend technology partnerships and stay engaged with industry forums to keep Micron at the forefront of enterprise AI.

Minimum Qualifications:
- Proven success delivering impact in generative AI/AI models and architecture roles, including leadership contributions across enterprise environments.

- Designing and deploying enterprise-scale generative AI/AI model platforms.

- 8+ years experience across cloud ecosystems (Azure/AWS/GCP), data engineering, and full MLOps lifecycle automation.

- Strong command of modern generative AI frameworks and tooling (PyTorch, TensorFlow, LangChain, vector databases) plus robust grounding in AI governance, security, privacy, and NIST AI RMF.

- Outstanding communicator skilled in executive-level storytelling, multi-functional influence, and quickly adopting and operationalizing emerging AI technologies.

Preferred Qualifications:
- Experience in semiconductor or manufacturing industries (understanding of MES, OT/IT integration, IP protection).

- Hands-on coding and prototyping ability in Python or similar, with familiarity of frontend technologies (for AI UX demos).

- Advanced degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field.

- Relevant certifications (e.g. Azure AI Engineer, Certified AI Professional).

- History of presenting at industry events or leading AI communities.

As a world leader in the semiconductor industry, Micron is dedicated to your personal wellbeing and professional growth. Micron benefits are designed to help you stay well, provide peace of mind and help you prepare for the future.  We offer a choice of medical, dental and vision plans in all locations enabling team members to select the plans that best meet their family healthcare needs and budget.  Micron also provides benefit programs that help protect your income if you are unable to work due to illness or injury, and paid family leave.  Additionally, Micron benefits include a robust paid time-off program and paid holidays.   For additional information regarding the Benefit programs available, please see the Benefits Guide posted on micron.com/careers/benefits .

Fab リーダーシップチームと密接に連携し、重要な Yield 関連プロジェクトおよびプログラムの企画・運営・管理を行うとともに、主要なプログラムリスクの特定およびエスカレーションを行います。

職務責任・業務内容
プログラム／プロジェクトマネジメント
- Speed に関する主要指標を含む戦略ロードマップを策定し、維持・更新を行うとともに、最新の BIC ターゲットに対する進捗を継続的に管理・追跡する
- 各プロジェクト／プログラムのビジネス価値および BIC 計画への貢献度を明確化するため、プロジェクトチームと連携して分析・整理を行う
- ビジネス計画の達成状況を可視化し、適切なリーダーシップレビューおよびチームミーティングの運営体制を構築・運用する
- プログラムおよびプロジェクトのパフォーマンスについて、部門横断的に定期報告および情報共有を行う
- スコープ、計画、ビジネスルール、ポリシー、手順等を含むプログラム変更を適切に管理・統制する
- サイトリーダーシップチームと協働し、プロジェクトリスクの特定、対策の立案および実行を主導する

ネットワーク連携
- Frontend SPMO ネットワーク、MCT、SEAL との協業において、担当カテゴリーにおけるサイト代表としての役割を担う
- サイトにとって価値のあるネットワークの BKM（Best Known Methods）および各種活動が確実に導入・実装されるよう推進する
- Frontend SPMO ネットワークと連携し、比較ベンチマーキングを実施するとともに、優良事例を迅速に横展開し、自サイトへのコピーおよび実装を行う
- MCT と連携し、PAC プロジェクトが計画されたスケジュール、スコープ、予算内で確実に実行されるよう管理する

[必須要件]
・工学系または理学系分野における学士号、もしくは同等の実務経験を有すること
・以下のいずれかの分野において 2年以上の実務経験を有すること：
- Frontend Fab Engineering（前工程Fabエンジニア）
- ビジネスアナリスト、マネジメント、またはファイナンス関連業務
- プログラム／プロジェクトマネジメントにおける実績ある経験

・高い分析力を有し、複雑な情報を簡潔かつ論理的に整理・説明できる能力
・優れたチームワーク力および複数業務を同時に遂行できるマルチタスク能力
・優れた文書作成能力および口頭コミュニケーション能力
・日本語または英語力がネイティブレベルの方。日本語ネイティブの場合、入社してから英語を学ぶ意欲がある方
AIを使用

・PIE、PEE、ATE の経験をお持ちの方

・同僚と円滑に協業し、オープンかつ明確なコミュニケーションを取ることができる能力
・優れたプロジェクト管理能力、時間管理能力、および優先順位設定スキル

Job Description
As a Speed PMO Engineer, you are responsible to enable Fab15 to set Best-in-Class performance on Yield metrics and transform the business to exceed yield business plans and commitments. You will be collaborating with fab leadership team to manage and run vital yield projects and programs as well as escalating key program risk.

Responsibilities and Tasks
Program/Project management
- Ensure strategic roadmaps with key metrics for Speed are created, maintained, and tracked to latest BIC targets.
- Collaborate with project teams to understand the business value of projects and programs in place and how they contribute to BIC plan.
- Visualize the progress of business plan achievement, and establish the meeting structure of appropriate leadership review and team meeting
- Provide program and project performance updates periodically with communication across functional groups.
- Manage and control program changes including scope, plan, business rules, policies, and procedures.

Network Engagement

- Ensure network BKMs and activities that are of value to your site are implemented

jobs.title: Global Accounting Operations Director
jobs.description:
Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all .
Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever.

Key Responsibilities

1) Value Realization & Capacity Release (Outcome Ownership)
- Owns end-to-end benefits realization for Accounting COE initiatives—converting productivity claims into sustained capacity release that can be redeployed to higher-value work and/or enable scalability.
- Establishes a practical approach to validate savings (run-rate vs one-time), prevent “benefit leakage,” and ensure improvements are embedded into standard operations and operating rhythms. (Recommended design; no additional source)
- Drives measurable improvement in COE operational outcomes (cycle time, productivity, stability, quality), aligned to COE strategic direction and efficiency ambitions.

2) Global Accounting COE Operational Performance (Run + Scale)
- Accountable for global operational health across Accounting COE services—ensuring stable delivery, scalable operating models, and consistent execution across regions.
- Ensures COE service commitments are translated into operating discipline, including SLA adherence, performance visibility, and corrective actions when service levels are at risk.
- Partners with functional leaders to reinforce standardization, operational readiness, and execution consistency that supports best-in-class performance.

3) Enterprise Advisory, Negotiation & Influence (E2E Beyond Accounting)
- Serves as the principal accounting advisor to enterprise process/system transformations (e.g., S2P and adjacent workflows), ensuring solutions are operationally feasible, scalable, and sustainable for Accounting execution.
- Influences senior stakeholders to drive timely decisions, resolve cross-functional conflicts, and secure end-to-end accountability across upstream/downstream partners.
- Negotiates trade-offs across speed, controls, cost, and operational capacity—balancing business outcomes with execution realities and control integrity.

4) Operational Risk, Controls Mindset & Issue Leadership
- Leads resolution of high-risk, high-visibility issues impacting operational continuity, control environment, or compliance readiness—especially those spanning regions/functions.
- Ensures operational changes strengthen effectiveness and reduce friction while maintaining a disciplined control mindset in execution.
- Applies structured problem-solving under ambiguity and time pressure; drives rapid containment and sustained fixes with clear ownership.

5) Benchmarking & Target-State Definition (External Lens)
- Brings external benchmarks and industry insights to challenge current practices, define target-state performance standards, and translate them into pragmatic roadmaps and operating model shifts.
- Helps advance COE toward “best-in-class” outcomes through scalable standards and measurable execution cadence.

6) Ad-Hoc Organizational & Cross-Functional Initiatives
- Undertakes ad-hoc organizational or cross-functional initiatives, including people‑related matters, as required to support operational priorities, resolve emerging issues, and ensure sustained performance across the Accounting COE

Key Interfaces / Stakeholders
- Accounting COE functional leaders (AP, GL, FA, etc.) for execution alignment and sustained adoption.
- Enterprise transformation stakeholders and upstream/downstream partners (e.g., Procurement/S2P, IT, Tax, Finance Ops) for E2E design tradeoffs and operationalization.
- COE performance framework partners where SLA/KPI commitments and service expectations are defined and tracked.

Qualifications
- Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field (CPA/CA preferred); MBA is an advantage.
- Typically 12–15+ years of experience in finance transformation, COE, or large-scale operations.
- Proven ability to influence senior leaders and drive decisions across functions and regions.
- Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional change in complex environments and operate effectively under ambiguity.
- Strong external perspective and strategic thinking; able to translate insights into executable roadmaps.

The US Construction Risk Manager plays a critical role in protecting project outcomes across a portfolio of large-scale construction programs. This position provides leadership in identifying, quantifying, monitoring, and mitigating risk throughout the project lifecycle. The successful candidate will work closely with project stakeholders to drive risk-informed decision making, support project execution, and provide executive-level insight into potential impacts to cost, schedule, safety, quality, and project delivery.

Responsibilities:
- Lead and continuously improve the construction risk management framework, including governance, risk identification, assessment, escalation, and reporting processes
- Own the program risk register, ensuring risks are quantified, assigned, actively managed, and tracked through closure
- Conduct quantitative schedule and cost risk analyses, including Monte Carlo simulations, contingency planning, and forecast development
- Partner with project teams, contractors, procurement, and stakeholders to develop and execute mitigation strategies for construction, supply chain, labor, contractual, and operational risks
- Deliver executive-level risk reporting, facilitate cross-functional risk reviews, and support informed decision making across the project portfolio

Minimum Qualifications:

- Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Architecture, or a related technical discipline
- 10+ years of experience in construction project controls, construction management, or capital project risk management, including direct responsibility for a formal risk management program
- Experience supporting large-scale capital construction projects valued at $1B+ within industrial, semiconductor, advanced manufacturing, data center, pharmaceutical, or similar environments
- Strong expertise in quantitative risk analysis, including Monte Carlo schedule and cost simulations, contingency development, and risk forecasting
- Working knowledge of construction contracts, claims management, project schedules, construction documents, OSHA construction standards, and AI tools such as Copilot or equivalent technologies

Preferred Qualifications:

- Master's degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Business Administration, or a related field
- Professional certification such as PMI-RMP, PMP, CCP, CEP, DRMP, CCM, or Professional Engineer (PE)
- Experience supporting semiconductor fabrication facility construction, including cleanrooms, process utility systems, central utility plants, or related infrastructure
- Experience with commissioning, production turnover readiness, integrated project delivery, advanced work packaging, or lean construction methodologies
- Proficiency with risk analytics and reporting tools such as Power BI or Tableau, including analysis of large project controls data sets and multi-site capital programs. Interest and/or experience in adaption of agentic AI into workflows and processes.

jobs.title: Logistics Security Program Manager - Asia Pacific Region
jobs.description:
Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all.

Join an inclusive team passionate about one thing: using their expertise in the relentless pursuit of innovation for customers and partners. The solutions we build help make everything from virtual reality experiences to breakthroughs in neural networks possible. We do it all while committing to integrity, sustainability, and giving back to our communities. Because doing so can fuel the very innovation we are pursuing.

The Logistics Security Program Manager plays a critical role in the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of Micron’s high-value logistics security program. This role is responsible for protecting high-value and high-risk shipments by defining risk-based logistics security controls, improving cargo-level visibility, monitoring carrier and third-party logistics provider performance, and coordinating escalation, response, and recovery activities across global transportation networks. The program manager will partner closely with Global Security, Supply Chain, Procurement, Logistics, Legal, Risk, and external logistics providers to ensure Micron maintains a scalable, auditable, and response-ready operating model for high-value shipments.  This role is specifically for program management of Micron’s logistics security in the Asia Pacific region.
Responsibilities
- Serve as a subject matter expert for high-value logistics security controls across global transportation lanes, carriers, freight forwarders, and third-party logistics providers.
- Develop, implement, and maintain a risk-based logistics security framework for high-value and high-risk shipments, considering shipment value, commodity attractiveness, route risk, geography, modality, dwell time, subcontracting, handoffs, theft history, and local recovery capability.
- Define baseline and enhanced security requirements for carriers and logistics providers, including cargo-level tracking, route compliance, approved stops, geofencing, chain of custody, tamper detection, monitoring, escalation, escorting, and recovery expectations.
- Partner with Procurement, Logistics, Global Security, Legal, and business stakeholders to embed logistics security requirements into carrier agreements, statements of work, operating procedures, and supplier performance expectations.
- Evaluate carrier, telematics, embedded tracking, smart seal, monitoring, and recovery solutions to ensure the architecture matches Micron’s security use cases and supports complex handoffs across truck, air, ocean, rail, brokered, and multimodal movements.
- Manage logistics security vendor reviews, pilots, and implementation activities, including device performance, coverage, air freight approvals, global execution constraints, integration requirements, monitoring center capabilities, and response service levels.
- Establish and oversee monitoring, escalation, and recovery workflows for high-value shipments, including alert validation, carrier and driver outreach, Micron notification, law-enforcement coordination, evidence preservation, and after-action review.
- Measure program effectiveness using outcome-based metrics such as shipment loss rate, response time, false-positive rate, missed escalation, carrier compliance, device failures, recovery performance, claims support, and security control maturity.
- Conduct carrier and lane risk assessments and recommend appropriate control overlays based on threat level, route complexity, aggregate shipment value, handoff exposure, and regional recovery capability.
- Support incident response for theft, diversion, tampering, route deviation, unauthorized stop, signal loss, seal breach, cargo separation, or other logistics security events involving Micron shipments.
- Develop and maintain logistics security policies, procedures, playbooks, standards, audit criteria, and governance materials aligned to recognized industry practices such as TAPA FSR/TSR or Micron-defined equivalents.
- Prepare executive-level briefings, risk summaries, program updates, supplier scorecards, and recommendations for senior leaders and cross-functional stakeholders.

Education
- Bachelor’s Degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Security Management, Criminal Justice, Business Administration, Risk Management, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field.
- Master’s degree or advanced professional education in supply chain, security, risk management, or business operations is a plus.
- Relevant certifications such as TAPA FSR/TSR, CPP, PSP, CTPAT, ASIS, supply chain risk, logistics, or security management certifications are preferred.

Experience
Experience developing, managing, or supporting logistics security, transportation risk, supply chain risk, cargo protection, physical security, or high-value shipment programs, with demonstrated experience in the following areas:
- High-value cargo security, logistics risk management, transportation security, carrier management, or supply chain security operations.
- Implementation or oversight of shipment security controls such as cargo-level tracking, telematics, geofencing, route management, approved stops, escorts, smart seals, tamper detection, monitoring, and incident escalation.
- Experience working with carriers, freight forwarders, 3PLs, security vendors, recovery providers, monitoring centers, or law-enforcement partners.
- Understanding of multimodal logistics operations, including truck, air, ocean, rail, cross-dock, customs, broker handoffs, final-mile movements, and other shipment separation events.
- Experience conducting route, lane, carrier, provider, or facility risk assessments and translating risk findings into practical control requirements.
- Experience managing vendor evaluations, statements of work, service-level expectations, operating procedures, supplier scorecards, and performance reviews.
- Knowledge of TAPA FSR/TSR, CTPAT, high-value cargo security practices, supply chain resilience, cargo theft trends, and incident response disciplines.
- Ability to analyze shipment risk data, carrier performance, alert activity, incident trends, and security metrics to drive continuous improvement.
- Experience coordinating cross-functionally with Procurement, Logistics, Global Security, Legal, Risk, business units, and external suppliers.
- Experience preparing executive-level communications, program recommendations, and incident summaries for senior leadership.

Soft Skills Requirements
- Ability to communicate logistics security risk in clear, business-relevant language for technical and non-technical stakeholders.
- Strong executive communication skills, including the ability to prepare concise briefings, recommendations, incident updates, and decision-ready materials.
- Ability to operate effectively in high-pressure, time-sensitive, and rapidly changing logistics or security incident environments.
- Strong analytical, problem-solving, and risk-based decision-making skills.
- Ability to build trusted partnerships with internal stakeholders, carriers, 3PLs, security providers, and external partners while maintaining clear accountability for security outcomes.
- Strong program management discipline, including the ability to manage multiple lanes, vendors, pilots, controls, and improvement initiatives simultaneously.
- Ability to balance security requirements with operational feasibility, cost, scalability, customer commitments, and business continuity needs.
- High attention to detail, sound judgment, discretion, and ability to handle confidential logistics, shipment, and security information appropriately.
- Ability to use AI-enabled tools to analyze logistics risk, identify trends, and support faster, well-governed decision-making.

Total Productive Management (TPM)

jobs.description:

The Logistics Security Program Manager plays a critical role in creating, applying, and improving Micron’s high-value logistics security efforts. This role centers on protecting high-value and high-risk shipments by defining risk-based security controls, boosting cargo-level visibility, tracking carrier and third-party logistics provider performance, and leading responses to customer concerns throughout global transportation networks. The program manager partners with Global Security, Supply Chain, Procurement, Logistics, Legal, Risk, and external logistics providers to ensure Micron operates a scalable, auditable, and response-ready model for high-value shipments. This role specifically covers program management in the Americas and Europe.

Responsibilities:

- Develop and uphold risk-focused logistics security frameworks and control strategies for valuable and sensitive shipments spanning various regions, routes, and transportation methods.

- Establish security requirements for carriers and logistics providers, including tracking, geofencing, chain of custody, tamper detection, monitoring, addressing critical issues, recovery, and compliance controls.

- Partner with Procurement, Logistics, Global Security, Legal, and business collaborators to integrate security requirements into contracts, operating procedures, supplier expectations, and governance processes.

- Evaluate and implement logistics security technologies and vendor solutions, including telematics, embedded tracking, smart seals, monitoring platforms, and recovery services across multimodal transportation networks.

- Lead logistics security vendor assessments, pilots, implementations, and ongoing performance management to ensure effective execution, integration, monitoring, and service delivery.

- Conduct carrier and lane risk assessments, manage incident response and recovery efforts, and coordinate monitoring, customer concern handling, law enforcement coordination, evidence preservation, and after-action reviews.

- Experience developing and managing logistics security, transportation risk, supply chain security, cargo protection, and high-value shipment programs with expertise in carrier management and security operations.

- Proven knowledge of shipment security controls, including cargo tracking, telematics, geofencing, route management, smart seals, tamper detection, monitoring, addressing critical issues, and recovery operations.

- Experience conducting risk assessments, managing vendors and supplier performance, analyzing security metrics and trends, and implementing continuous improvement initiatives across multimodal logistics networks.

- Strong understanding of industry security frameworks (TAPA, CTPAT), cargo theft prevention, incident response, and working closely with Procurement, Logistics, Global Security, Legal, business leaders, external partners, and executive collaborators.

About our Team:

As an IT Disaster Recovery Program Manager within Micron's Governance, Risk, Compliance, and Cyber Resilience organization, you will serve as the subject matter expert responsible for the design, governance, execution, and continuous improvement of Micron's global Information Technology Disaster Recovery (ITDR) program. Our team partners closely with Infrastructure, Applications, Cybersecurity, Business Continuity Management (BCM), Engineering, Manufacturing, Cloud Operations, Site Leadership, and Executive Stakeholders to build and maintain enterprise resilience. Together, we help ensure critical business services can be restored within established Recovery Time Objectives (RTOs) and Recovery Point Objectives (RPOs) while supporting regulatory and cyber resilience requirements.

Position Overview:

This role leads enterprise recovery planning, resilience assessments, disaster recovery exercises, recovery capability validation, and executive reporting to strengthen organizational readiness and operational continuity. The IT Disaster Recovery Program Manager drives preparedness against cyber attacks, ransomware events, infrastructure failures, operational disruptions, and natural disasters while aligning recovery strategies with business requirements and compliance obligations. In addition, you will contribute to AI-enabled resilience initiatives by leveraging automation, analytics, and intelligent workflows to improve recovery planning, dependency mapping, exercise execution, and resilience reporting.

Responsibilities:
- Lead the design, governance, execution, and continuous improvement of Micron's global Information Technology Disaster Recovery (ITDR) program.

- Develop and execute enterprise recovery planning, resilience assessments, disaster recovery exercises, recovery testing programs, and resilience validation activities.

- Partner with Infrastructure, Applications, Cybersecurity, Business Continuity Management (BCM), Engineering, Manufacturing, Cloud Operations, Site Leadership, and Executive Stakeholders to align recovery strategies with business requirements, regulatory obligations, and cyber resilience objectives.

- Drive enterprise readiness against operational disruptions, cyber attacks, ransomware events, infrastructure failures, and natural disasters through governance, metrics, testing, and continuous improvement.

- Contribute to AI-enabled resilience initiatives by applying automation, analytics, and workflow technologies to improve resilience program effectiveness and efficiency.

Minimum Qualifications:
- Bachelor's degree required.

- 8+ years of experience in disaster recovery, business continuity, information security, infrastructure operations, cyber resilience, or related fields.

- 5+ years of experience managing enterprise resilience, recovery, or risk management programs.

- Strong hands-on experience leading enterprise Disaster Recovery (DR), Business Continuity (BC), Cyber Resilience, or Infrastructure Resilience programs.

- Demonstrated experience developing and executing disaster recovery exercises, recovery testing programs, and resilience validation activities.

Preferred Qualifications:
- Strong understanding of recovery architecture including cloud services, infrastructure platforms, identity systems, backup technologies, networking, and critical enterprise applications, with working knowledge of RTO, RPO, Business Impact Analysis (BIA), and technology dependency mapping.

- Experience supporting audit activities and regulatory compliance initiatives involving resilience and recovery controls, including ISO 27001, NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF), TISAX, SOX, and other applicable resilience requirements.

jobs.description:
Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all .
Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever.

We are seeking a Senior Manager with 10+ years of experience to lead the Supply Chain Planning Intelligence team within our Enterprise Planning Solutions (EPS) organization, part of Micron’s IT Enterprise AI function. This is not a traditional supply chain applications role—it is a planning transformation leadership role.

In this position, you will lead a hybrid team of Industry Analysts, Data Scientists, and Solution Architects to build and scale the intelligence layer across Micron’s supply chain planning ecosystem. Your team will focus on making planning smarter, faster, and increasingly autonomous, independent of the underlying tools or platforms.

Responsibilities:
- AI-Led Planning Transformation (Primary Focus): Define and own the Planning Intelligence roadmap — what decisions Applications Teams should be automating, augmenting, or accelerating with AI in the next 12–24 months. Lead adoption of Generative AI, agentic workflows, and evolving AI tools across supply chain planning domains. Identify and scale high-impact use cases — exception-based planning, AI scenario generation, natural-language planning insights, decision journaling. Drive end-to-end AI lifecycle from problem framing through PoC to production deployment. Ensure AI capabilities improve actual planning outcomes — fill rates, decision latency, manual effort reduction — not just deployment counts. Define the architecture for a unified Planning Intelligence layer that works with or without specific planning tools underneath.

- EPS Team Integration & Org Collaboration: Earn trust from an existing team of Business Analysts, Software Engineers, and Solution Architects who have deep SAP, Kinaxis and Blue Yonder expertise. Apply the team's intake rule: no planning AI or analytics work starts without a named decision owner, identified execution system, and assigned data product owner. Partner with Data Engineering and Analytics Ops teams to consume governed Snowflake data products for every planning initiative.

- Executive Leadership: Act as the primary interface between Supply Chain business leaders, IT Enterprise AI leadership, and the EPS organization. Translate AI capabilities into planning business value — present in terms of clear and measurable outcomes, not model accuracy. Enable executive visibility with clear objectives and key results. Partner with planning teams globally to ensure AI solutions reflect ground-level planning reality.

- Team Leadership & Capability Building: Lead and grow a hybrid team of Industry Analysts, Data Scientists, and Solution Architects. Build a culture of outcome ownership — every AI initiative owns its business metric, not just its technical delivery. Develop the team's ability to operate at the boundary of AI and supply chain planning — a rare and high-value set of skills.

Minimum Qualifications:
- Sufficient understanding of supply chain planning concepts — demand, supply, inventory, order promising, IBP — to frame AI problems accurately

- Proven experience leading AI, GenAI, or advanced analytics programs from ideation to production at scale

- Strong understanding of AI/ML architectures, agentic systems, and LLM-based workflows

- Familiarity with planning platforms (Blue Yonder, Kinaxis, SAP IBP) as context for embedding AI

- Understanding of modern data platforms (Snowflake, data products, semantic layers)

Preferred Qualifications:
- Familiarity with enterprise AI tooling — LLM platforms, Copilot, agentic frameworks

- Curiosity about how AI can reshape planning workflows beyond what current tools support

- Strong Agile delivery expertise — roadmap management, prioritization, risk management

- Ability to engage credibly with Data Scientists and Solution Architects on architecture and design decisions

jobs.title: Sr Manager, Procurement Platform Excellence
jobs.description:
Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all .
Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever.

Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all.
Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever.
The Global Procurement team is an integral engine to Micron’s growth, delivering best-in-class total cost and supply chain resiliency through innovative predictive capabilities, risk analysis, and a focus on sustainability and diversity. Our business goals are directly tied to the value we place on our team members, our greatest asset. We invest in our people through a skills-based learning and development model to create clear career pathways for growth. Join us and discover why Micron’s Global Procurement team is the preferred destination to ignite your talent.
As Senior Manager, Platform Excellence within Global Procurement’s Center of Excellence Digital Transformation & AI organization, you drive the Source-to-Pay (S2P) platform strategy and roadmap and lead end-to-end management of the S2P platform landscape. This is a collaborative role: you shape one coherent S2P platform direction together with your peer Senior Managers for S/4HANA Transformation, AI Transformation, Data & Process Automation, and Data Excellence & Governance. Your portfolio spans sourcing, contract lifecycle management, procure-to-pay, supplier and catalog enablement, and the analytics and reporting platforms used by the data analytics team, and you lead a team based in Hyderabad, India.
This is not a SAP or ERP configuration role. The SAP S/4HANA and Ariba transformation is driven by a separate team; you partner closely with them so the S2P platform landscape integrates cleanly with the ERP core and enterprise systems, and every platform decision reinforces one coherent, standardized S2P experience. Similarly, new AI transformation products that are still at an early, incubation stage sit with the AI Transformation team — your accountability is the established S2P platform portfolio and how it is run, integrated, and adopted.
You set direction and priorities and own value realization measured in real business terms — productivity, adoption, cycle time, and decision quality. You bring strong product and user-centered discipline to how the portfolio is run: grounding decisions in user personas, journeys, and end-to-end processes, and owning supplier-supported and third-party products end-to-end, including escalation, supplier performance (reviews, SLAs, demos), licensing, renewals, and end-of-life transitions.
This is a people-leadership role. A core part of your mandate is to move platform operations from reactive, ticket-driven support to a proactive, agent-embedded model, and to embed product and user-centered discipline across the portfolio. You develop a team of platform and product professionals and partner closely with AI Transformation, Data & Process Automation, Data Excellence & Governance, IT, Enterprise Architecture, Security, and Compliance. GP-centric platform products are owned here end-to-end; enterprise-wide systems and IT infrastructure remain with IT — the role does not perform software development or manage infrastructure.
▍ Key Responsibilities
A core expectation is to run Global Procurement’s Source-to-Pay platforms as products — end-to-end, value-driven, well-integrated, and adopted — while moving platform operations toward a proactive, agent-embedded model.
Platform Strategy & Value Optimization
- Own the end-to-end S2P platform portfolio strategy and roadmap — including the analytics and reporting platforms — framing business problems into clear product strategies that maximize outcomes over outputs.
- Prioritize opportunities and make build-versus-buy-versus-partner trade-offs, sequencing platform investment against S2P Reimagined and ERP transformation milestones.
- Track value through real business indicators — productivity, adoption, cycle time, and decision quality — and engage stakeholders on investment decisions and supplier and technology trends.

End-to-End Platform Leadership & Lifecycle
- Lead and be accountable for the S2P platform portfolio across its full lifecycle — sourcing, contract lifecycle management, procure-to-pay, supplier and catalog enablement, and analytics platforms — setting clear direction and adapting priorities as needs evolve.
- Own supplier-supported and third-party products for GP-centric solutions, including escalation, supplier performance management (reviews, SLAs, demos), licensing, renewals, and end-of-life transitions.
- Apply product-management fundamentals — budgeting, cost-versus-value trade-offs, and lifecycle planning — to keep platforms fit-for-purpose as scale and complexity grow, while keeping GP-centric solutions PM-owned and enterprise-wide systems with IT.

Platform Operations, Integration & Health
- Own platform stability, configuration, release, environment and test, and incident and problem management across the S2P landscape.
- Ensure the S2P platforms integrate cleanly with the SAP S/4HANA and Ariba ERP core and enterprise systems, so data, controls, and processes flow reliably end-to-end.
- Establish platform health KPIs, service levels, and monitoring, and shift from reactive support to proactive, increasingly self-healing platforms — with agents handling detection, triage, routing, and routine configuration and testing.

Analytics Platforms, Adoption & Product Performance
- Product-manage the analytics and reporting platforms used by the data analytics team — ensuring the tooling is reliable, well-integrated, and fit-for-purpose, while analytics outputs and insights remain owned by the data analytics team.
- Instrument platforms to measure usage, adoption, and value, and use those signals to refine roadmaps and features.
- Define what “good adoption” means beyond usage — decision confidence, reduced rework, and behavior change.

User-Centered Solution Design
- Ground solutions in user personas, journeys, and end-to-end process understanding, balancing usability, feasibility, business value, and enterprise constraints.
- Challenge low-value features and over-customization; advocate scalable, standard-driven design and consistent interaction patterns across S2P tools and AI-enabled capabilities.
- Anticipate adoption risks and continuously improve solutions based on user behavior and usage signals.

Stakeholder Engagement, Enablement & Change
- Engage stakeholders, build trust, and bring people along through change; translate needs into clear action plans and resolve issues through influence and partnership.
- Own the platform enablement and support model — training, documentation, self-service, and a responsive support experience across regions.
- Embed change management into the product journey and drive adoption through clear, simple, actionable communication.

Innovation & Agent-Embedded Ways of Working
- Reimagine platform operations and enablement with agents embedded — platform support copilot, configuration and testing agents, integration-monitoring agents, and enablement copilot.
- Sponsor rapid experiments, validate impact, and turn the best into reusable building blocks for broader adoption across Source-to-Pay.

Team Leadership & Enterprise Partnership
- Lead, coach, and develop a Hyderabad-based team; build depth, ownership, and succession, and coach the team for a product-led, agent-embedded operating model.
- Partner across DTAI pillars, IT, Enterprise Architecture, Security, Compliance, and functional Global Procurement teams, and represent the platform agenda in program reviews and executive readouts.
- Serve as the primary escalation point for platform stability, integration, and adoption risks, translating complex dynamics into clear decisions and tradeoffs for senior stakeholders.

▍ Leadership Expectations
This leader is expected to embody Micron’s core values and set the tone for the team:
People
Care for each other — build an inclusive, high-trust team; develop talent, grow capability, and plan succession within the team.
Innovation
Shape the future — run platforms as products and champion agent-embedded ways of working; experiment, learn fast, and scale what works.
Tenacity
Nothing shakes our resolve — own platform stability, integration, and adoption outcomes end-to-end through complex, cross-system challenges.
Collaboration
Aligned to win — break silos across DTAI, IT, Enterprise Architecture, Security, and the business; win as one team across time zones.
Customer Focus
Partner and win together — treat procurement stakeholders and end-users as customers; design for their journeys and deliver adopted, high-value platforms.
Speed
Act with purpose and set the pace — make timely, well-reasoned decisions and move prioritized platform work from pilot to scale without losing rigor.

▍ Leadership Competencies
- Product & value judgment: Frame problems into value-driven strategy, prioritize outcomes over outputs, and make build-versus-buy-versus-partner calls with clarity.
- User-centered & adoption mindset: Design for real user journeys and adoption, not just delivery, and define value beyond usage.
- Talent & coaching: Develop, coach, and grow a multi-region team; build bench strength and succession within the function.
- Cross-cultural leadership: Work effectively across U.S. and Asia cultures and time zones, partnering with globally distributed stakeholders and peers.
- Influence & partnership: Lead through influence across IT, Enterprise Architecture, Security, and business stakeholders without direct authority.
- Executive communication: Translate complex platform, integration, and product topics into crisp, decision-ready narratives for senior leaders.
- Change leadership: Drive adoption of new platforms and agent-embedded ways of working through enablement and change management.
- Outcome ownership: Set direction, prioritize ruthlessly, and hold the function accountable for measurable stability, adoption, and value.

▍ Minimum Requirements
- Education: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Engineering, Supply Chain, Business, or a related field.
- Experience — depth: 13+ years in enterprise platform, digital product, or Source-to-Pay application management, including 5+ years leading platform or digital product delivery and operations and 3+ years leading teams.
- Experience — scale: At least 5 years in a large, multi-region enterprise (5,000+ employees), including environments running on SAP (ECC and/or S/4HANA).
- Experience — domain: Deep, hands-on ownership of a Source-to-Pay platform landscape (several of sourcing, contract lifecycle management, procure-to-pay, supplier and catalog enablement, and procurement analytics platforms), with close working knowledge of how these integrate with an SAP S/4HANA and Ariba ERP core.
- Product management: Proven end-to-end product ownership — vision, roadmap, prioritization, and value realization — with a track record of driving outcomes over outputs.
- Supplier / third-party product management: Managing supplier-supported products, including escalation, SLAs, performance reviews, licensing, renewals, and end-of-life transitions.
- Analytics & adoption: Working knowledge of analytics and business intelligence (Power BI or Tableau) and of instrumenting products to measure adoption and value.
- Integration: Proven experience integrating SaaS platforms with an ERP core — APIs, middleware, connectors, and cross-system data and controls.
